source.locator: dist/index.d.mts ISystemDependencyFactories/ISetupDcouplrConfig, lines 178–218; dist/index-C3YI4Tf9.d.mts IDFactory, lines 771–779, inspector options, lines 938–959; dist/index.mjs withVerifiedFactoryOutput, buildSystemDependencies, validateKernelFactoryInput and setupDcouplr, lines 3377–3386, 3480–3622; dist/inspector/index.mjs startDcouplrInspector and resolveDebugConsoleOptions
source.paraphrase: Setup and inspector options use the public keys and types. Inspector numeric options must be finite. Each supplied system override is an IDFactory with a string __semanticIdentifier and synchronous callable create.

invariants.why: Invalid literal bootstrap options or factories reject initialization/resolution or are silently ignored. Missing charEncoding and factory identifiers are tolerated by this runtime but violate the public required-field contracts. Unknown literal keys can hide a misspelled setting. Async/generator create returns do not satisfy the synchronous system-factory output contracts. Infinity and NaN event budgets disable bounded retention; a negative infinite budget discards every event.
invariants.fixHint: Supply charEncoding and use the public setup fields and types. Use only Logger, EventBus, MessageBus, DCast, IQueue, IQueuePersistence, MessageBrokerAdapter and EventBrokerAdapter system overrides. Each supplied factory needs a string __semanticIdentifier and synchronous callable create; its output must satisfy that system contract. Inspector host/instanceId/path are strings, port/maxEvents are finite numbers, and captureOnStart/announce/enabled are booleans. Use object options for startDcouplrInspector; only setup's inspector also accepts a boolean. Choose mode and ephemeral for the actual runtime; keep dynamic configurations, output behavior and inspector access/resource limits under a project verifier. Use only supported forbiddenElements.
invariants.avoid: Reserved setupDcouplr/startDcouplrInspector call-name policy in reviewed paths, not import/receiver identity or whole-program setup/get order. Direct identifier/dot/literal-bracket calls and transparent wrappers are checked. Plain object fields use the last duplicate key at configuration, system-override, factory, inspector and debug-console levels; optional undefined, shorthand and dynamic values stay valid or unresolved. Spread/computed/getter/method/prototype/escaped-key configurations are deferred. Direct inspector options follow the second argument, unless the first is a spread. Known wrong literal field types, bigint numeric values and unknown keys reject; absent options and optional fields remain valid. Direct Infinity/NaN, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY/NEGATIVE_INFINITY/NaN and globalThis.Infinity/NaN reject, including literal brackets and unary/value wrappers. A binding containing Infinity, NaN, Number or globalThis anywhere in the file, escaped binding text, or with defers those global predicates conservatively; this is not lexical resolution. Arithmetic, overflow literals, aliases, wrapped receivers, dynamic global changes, integer/range validity and class field values remain unresolved. Compatible static inspector/debug-console class options remain unresolved. Network binding, actual production mode, authorization, lifecycle and complete recording limits remain unverified. Literal factories check required __semanticIdentifier/create and known invalid types, including async/generator creators. The identifier need not equal a reserved system key: dictionary registration owns that key. Static class factories can satisfy the public structural contract and remain unresolved. Named/aliased factory shape, indirect asynchronous creators, actual output member/behavior contracts and escaped or dynamic enum strings are unresolved. Omitting ephemeral remains valid: the pinned setup path forwards undefined, so this rule does not promise the documented true default or broker delivery guarantees.

source.paraphrase: Bootstrap settings and instanceId are system-owned and must not be overwritten through settings.setSetting.

invariants.why: The runtime refuses to overwrite a key in its system configuration even when its bootstrap value is undefined. Mode, encoding, delivery settings, forbidden elements and instance identity belong to setup.
invariants.fixHint: Set system options once in setupDcouplr. Use settings.setSetting only for application runtime keys and read system values with getSetting/getMode.
invariants.avoid: Direct settings.setSetting receiver-shape policy in reviewed paths, not inferred IDKernel types. Covers the five pinned system keys with dot/literal-bracket/optional calls, transparent wrappers and literal keys. Detached settings/setter aliases, dynamic/escaped keys, custom bootstrap fields and unrelated receiver identities remain unresolved. The rule does not prohibit application-owned settings or prove setup occurs exactly once.

source.work: dcouplr 0.1.3-beta published runtime; explicit PREGATE project policy
source.locator: dist/index.mjs SystemDependencyKeys, DcouplrInternal constructor and #warnIfKernelIsRegisteredThroughAdmission, lines 675–689, 768–840, 1068–1071
source.paraphrase: DKERNEL is bootstrap-owned runtime infrastructure and must not be registered through public dependency admission.

invariants.why: Public kernel admission can reject as a duplicate or create a second kernel registration while managed factories still receive the bootstrap kernel. The runtime warns that this infrastructure is bootstrap-owned.
invariants.fixHint: Remove the DKERNEL admission. Configure the supported system factories at setup and receive IDKernel as the factory's injected second argument.
invariants.avoid: Reserved method/key policy in the selected paths, not receiver-type inference. Direct fluent register/registerSingleton/registerForce/registerSingletonForce chains cover literal DKERNEL and direct DependencyKeys.Kernel access, dot/literal-bracket/optional calls, parentheses and transparent as/satisfies/non-null wrappers. Only receiver links are followed; nested callbacks, arguments, strings and createOnly are not registrations. Tests have no ownership exemption. Named handles, function/key aliases, computed/escaped names, arbitrary chain methods and bootstrap order remain unresolved. Review narrower paths if an unrelated API uses the same reserved names. Runtime warnings and partial admission do not establish a safe kernel replacement.

source.work: dcouplr 0.1.3-beta published runtime; explicit PREGATE project policy
source.paraphrase: Force admission is available only when the runtime mode is test.

invariants.why: Production replacement bypasses normal duplicate-ownership checks and the runtime rejects it outside test mode.
invariants.fixHint: Use register/registerSingleton in production. Keep force replacement in reviewed test modules with mode: test.
invariants.avoid: Explicit method-name policy reserves registerForce/registerSingletonForce calls in the reviewed production paths; it does not infer receiver types. Dot, optional and unescaped literal bracket/template calls are covered. A project with an unrelated API of the same name must narrow paths or review an exception. Detached function aliases, computed names, escaped literals and actual runtime mode are not resolved; an excluded test file does not prove test mode.

invariants.why: Production code must not import dcouplr test reset or test runtime helpers.
invariants.fixHint: Keep test helpers in test modules. Initialize the production runtime once at the application boundary.
invariants.avoid: Value named imports and direct namespace dot/bracket references and object destructuring are checked. Type-only imports, shadowed namespaces, legitimate bootstrap and excluded test files are admitted. Namespace aliases, computed members, dynamic/CommonJS imports and re-export barrels remain gaps; nested-block var hoisting remains conservative.
